newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - WASHINGTON POST BUSINESS - AUG 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - WASHINGTON POST BUSINESS - AUG 13.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following items on the front page of its business section on Aug. 13:
WASHINGTON - The AFL-CIO federation of unions pledged $10 million a week in support of the Teamsters striking United Parcel Service.
HAVERFORD, PENNSYLVANIA - Entrepeneurial teens are spending their summer at a camp designed to teach them the ins and outs of business and how to compete at sports like golf, tennis and squash.
WASHINGTON - UPS remains the kind of company run by people who started at the bottom and worked their way up.
WASHINGTON - U.S. District Judge Royce Lamberth cleared the way for a class action age discrimination suit against First American Bank.
NEW YORK - U.S. stocks dropped sharply as a report pointing to a pickup in consumer spending this month stirred inflation fears and sent interest rates rising again in the bond market.
